title: Agent-DLC with AgentCore Launchpad: Run the Agent Development Lifecycle from One Console
html:
What problem this workshop solves

Getting an agent to demo well is easy. Taking it into production with confidence is hard. Teams adopting agents keep asking the same four questions:

  1. Are the answers reliable?
  2. Is it safe and compliant?
  3. Will we catch problems before users do?
  4. After a prompt change, did it get better or worse?

The root causes: agent behavior is non-deterministic, the prompt is the system, and models can be updated silently. One-off acceptance testing no longer works. The hard part is not model quality — it is steering the agent and proving it meets the bar.

Agent-DLC (Agent Development Lifecycle) is an evaluation-centric method: turn every requirement into a measurable criterion, then run a continuous flywheel that makes the agent better with every turn.

What you will use

This workshop is built on AgentCore Launchpad, an open-source agent operations platform. One React console over one FastAPI backend wires Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, Harness, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Registry, Policy, Evaluation and Observability into a single create → deploy → invoke → observe experience. Everything runs against real resources in the AWS account the organiser prepared for your team — no mocks.

Write the agent with Strands Agents, run it reliably on AgentCore, and manage its whole lifecycle with Launchpad.

The Agent-DLC flywheel

flowchart LR
  D[Define] --> B[Build] --> E[Evaluate] --> R[Release] --> O[Observe] --> F[Improve]
  F --> D
Phase Question it answers Launchpad feature Who does it
Define What does "good" look like? Criteria table (five dimensions; red line / gate / observe tiers; sign-off), golden set (dev / regression / holdout splits), custom evaluators developer drafts; biz-owner signs and seals the holdout
Build How is the agent written and deployed? Strands ZIP, managed Harness, container / BYOC; Knowledge Bases, Registry, Memory developer
Evaluate Does it meet the bar today? Cost estimate and caps, pass^k, gate report, judge calibration (κ) developer runs; developer + sme annotate; biz-owner decides calibration
Release How do we ship safely? Gated release (candidate → live), waivers, rollback, public API (/v1/...), Cedar policies at the Gateway, A/B and canary release-ops signs releases and approves waivers
Observe What is happening in production? Observability dashboard and traces, spend and alerts, intents view, drift watch, scorecard, decision history Everyone
Improve How does the next round get better? Issue box (thumbs-down, expert corrections through a reviewer link) → sample admission → golden regression split → fix ladder → next criteria version; online evaluation keeps scoring real sessions sme corrects; biz-owner admits; developer drafts the next version

Lab scenario: customer service for a multi-line consumer platform

Every lab is built around Unicorn Company, a fictional consumer platform with two business lines:

  • Retail and e-commerce (Unicorn Mall): an online store plus physical shops. Service handles product questions, stock and pricing, orders and shipping, returns and exchanges.
  • Travel (OTA, Unicorn Trip): flights on the fictional Unicorn Air and rooms at the fictional Unicorn Hotels. Service handles flight lookups, changes and refunds, baggage allowance, hotel bookings and cancellation policies.

You will build two agents for it, plus two optional ones:

Agent Creation method Role
lab-service-assistant Strands ZIP path Main line: a single service entry point that detects intent, explains return, flight change/refund and cancellation rules from the policy knowledge base and computes fees; used through evaluation, release and observation
lab-policy-advisor Managed Harness Grounded Q&A over a policy knowledge base (e-commerce return rules, airline change/refund and baggage policy, hotel cancellation terms)
lab-legacy-agent BYOC (optional) Migrates a tool-calling LangChain agent for refund, change and baggage rules to Strands Agents and deploys it on AgentCore Runtime
lab-legacy-container Container (optional) Deploys a trip-planning assistant as a Claude Agent SDK container

What the five quality dimensions mean here:

Dimension Retail / e-commerce OTA / flights / hotels
🧠 Cognition Tells apart return rules across categories and stacking rules across promotions Tells apart change/refund rules across fare classes and cancellation windows across hotels
✅ Quality Order and shipping status match the system; refund amounts are correct Answers match policy documents; change/refund fees are correct
🛡️ Responsibility Never leaks shipping addresses or phone numbers; never changes prices or refunds without authorization Never leaks traveler ID numbers; never issues tickets or refunds without authorization
💰 Cost Tokens per inquiry; whether a smaller model can handle simple lookups Same
⚡ Performance Latency and concurrency during sales events Latency and concurrency during holiday travel peaks

All companies, products, airlines, hotels, orders and policies in the scenario are fictional sample data.

Working as a team: five lab accounts

The heart of Agent-DLC is separation of duties: whoever writes the standard cannot sign it, whoever annotates cannot decide the calibration, and whoever requests a release cannot approve it. The lab environment comes with five accounts (the organiser gives your team their passwords), and you will switch between them across chapters:

Account Role Duty in the flywheel
admin Administrator Approves registrations, creates departments / projects and assigns project roles, platform configuration, manages the release policy
developer Member Builds and deploys agents, drafts and publishes criteria, runs evaluations
biz-owner Member (business owner) Signs criteria, curates the golden set and admissions, decides judge calibration
release-ops Operator Moves agents to named endpoints, signs releases, approves waivers
sme Member (subject-matter expert) Second annotator for calibration, submits corrections through a reviewer link

Use one normal browser window plus a few private/incognito windows (or separate browser profiles) to stay signed in as several accounts at once.

Who it is for

  • Developers building, or planning to build, AI agents — with or without an existing prototype.
  • No AWS account, AWS console or AWS credentials needed: the organiser deploys every team's environment in advance, and everything runs in the browser. Only the public API section of the Release chapter uses curl in your own terminal, with an API key the console issues, not AWS credentials.
  • Teams of 4–5 people per business line work best.

How to walk this workshop

The chapters come in three groups; take them in order:

  1. Before You Start — method, environment, roles, teams and projects, platform configuration. After this group the team works in the project 零售客服 (retail service, retail-service) on one console, every role has a person, and the workspace release mode is gated.
  2. The Agent-DLC Flywheel — phases 1 to 6, each one building on the same customer-service agent. The phases depend on each other's state, so keep the order.
  3. Team Lab and Wrap-up — run the loop again on your own scenario, then clean up.

How the organiser deploys the environments before the event and tears them down afterwards is in Appendix · Organizer deployment guide; online update, single sign-on and private networking for running the console afterwards are in Appendix · Platform operations; participants need neither. When a term is unfamiliar during the lab (criteria, golden set, gate …), look it up in Appendix · Glossary.

Duration

About 1.5 days: Day 1 morning covers method and architecture, Day 1 afternoon is hands-on in teams, Day 2 morning is team demos and discussion. Each chapter can also run on its own as a 2–4 hour lab.
